xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2356: Directory and relay service: services/connect, direct connections, relay add-on and webhook inbox

plan.title: Directory and relay service: services/connect, direct connections, relay add-on and webhook inbox
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The operator's epic (pan-2350.md, Issue disposition) assigns W-LINK5, W-LINK8 and the directory inbox of W-INT1 to this one issue. All three are served by one Cloudflare Worker (services/connect), one Durable Object class, one wire protocol (packages/contracts/src/connect.ts) and one machine-side directory client, so sibling issues would serialize on the same files and could not be verified separately: the Done-when checks need the Worker and the client together (D-2356-20). The plan is decomposed into 24 independently reviewable items instead.

narratives.Problem: Two Overdeck machines on different networks without Tailscale cannot reach each other, and a webhook trigger loses every event sent while its machine is offline. PAN-4645 built the secure channel and the link supervisor; nothing provides the overdeck.ai directory, peer-to-peer routes, a relay fallback or an inbox (verified on main 1c20fe2c38b).
narratives.Proposal: Build services/connect, a Cloudflare Worker with one AccountDirectory Durable Object per account: presence and a per-plan machine limit (3 on the free plan), signalling for WebRTC, TURN credentials with monthly metering and a 50 GB cap for relay-plan accounts, and a webhook inbox that seals each event to the machine key and keeps only sealed bytes for at most 24 hours. On the machine, add a directory client, a werift WebRTC transport carrying the existing Noise secure channel as rtc:// (direct) and rtc+turn:// (relay) dynamic routes probed after LAN/Tailscale routes, a two-screen approval flow that links account machines without a pairing code, the relay status on the Anywhere card, and inbox delivery into the PAN-4648 trigger core.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Billing, Creem products or a working Add 50 GB purchase (PAN-4294); the button only links to https://overdeck.ai/anywhere
- Opening overdeck.ai sign-up to non-allowlisted GitHub users
- Deploying services/connect or services/account to Cloudflare, or running the live cross-network checks (operator checkpoint, D-2356-21)
- Persisting rtc:// or rtc+turn:// routes in machine-links.json
- Any change to services/share or Shared Sessions
- pan connect / npx @overdeck/core connect (PAN-4656)
- Webhook trigger features beyond the inbox flag: Funnel delivery, signature checks and pan triggers management stay as PAN-4648 built them
- A Settings UI field for anywhere.directory_url
- Per-gigabyte billing, relay for free accounts, or multi-region relay selection
- Directory machines in the conversation sidebar or fleet views (PAN-4650)
- Any edit to src/cli/index.ts, src/lib/settings-api.ts or src/dashboard/server/main.ts

autoDecisions.summary: Free plan comes from the existing grants.entitlement column: 'free' maps to { plan: 'free', maxDevices: 3 }; everything else stays 'tester' (D-2356-3).
autoDecisions.rationale: The account service is invite-only and has only plan 'tester'; this makes the 3-machine limit testable without opening public sign-up, and OD-3 says paid tiers stay allowlist-only until billing.

autoDecisions.summary: Approval needs confirmation on both machines with a six-digit code from the Noise XX handshake hash (D-2356-9/10), tightening FR-20's one-sided approval.
autoDecisions.rationale: D-18 forbids a compromised directory making any machine trust an impostor; a one-sided approval leaves the new machine trusting whoever approves it. Numeric comparison closes that gap at the cost of one extra click.

autoDecisions.summary: direct and relay routes are dynamic, provided by the directory client and never written to machine-links.json (D-2356-7).
autoDecisions.rationale: link-store isRoute rejects unknown schemes and a rejected file empties every link, so persisting rtc:// would drop all links on a downgrade.

autoDecisions.summary: Probing runs in three phases: LAN/tailnet/public at 2.5 s, then direct at 10 s, then relay at 10 s (D-2356-8).
autoDecisions.rationale: WebRTC setup across NAT cannot finish in 2.5 s, and FR-21 requires the relay only when every other route failed; phasing also avoids WebRTC negotiation while LAN works.

autoDecisions.summary: The relay channel initiator reports ciphertext bytes every 60 s and on close; the cap stops new TURN credentials (600 s TTL) and broadcasts stopped (D-2356-12). Add 50 GB links to https://overdeck.ai/anywhere.
autoDecisions.rationale: One reporter per channel avoids double counting; the account's own machines are already trusted with its data; billing is out of scope.

autoDecisions.summary: Inbox URL is /h/<doId>.<secret> with a 256 KiB body cap, 200 pending events per inbox and 64 MiB per account (D-2356-13/14).
autoDecisions.rationale: Encoding the Durable Object id routes without a global index; each sealed event must fit one WebSocket message after base64.

autoDecisions.summary: Sealed box: Worker seals with pinned @noble 2.4.0 libraries, machine opens with sodium-native 5.2.0 crypto_box_seal_open, proven by a fixed-vector interop test (D-2356-16).
autoDecisions.rationale: D-20 names an X25519 sealed box; libsodium is the reference implementation and sodium-native is already in the lockfile via the Noise stack.

autoDecisions.summary: werift pinned at 0.25.1 and bundled; one peer connection per (peer, kind) with a data channel per secure-channel connection (D-2356-11).
autoDecisions.rationale: The epic chose werift; 0.25.1 is the newest release older than two weeks; LinkAgent pools up to four channels per machine.

autoDecisions.summary: Inbox delivery skips only the URL-secret step of the trigger core and measures the Stripe 300 s tolerance against the sealed receivedAt (D-2356-17).
autoDecisions.rationale: The inbox secret already authorised the sender, and a 24-hour hold would otherwise fail every Stripe signature.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep all three work items in one plan with plan.metadata.sizeJustification (D-2356-20).
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator's epic assigns them to this issue and they share one Worker, Durable Object, protocol and client.

autoDecisions.summary: anywhere.directory_url is read straight from config.yaml with no Settings UI field (D-2356-19).
autoDecisions.rationale: settings-api.ts is over the file-size ceiling; Settings saves preserve unknown YAML blocks (setBlockMergePreserving).

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5, D-2356-2/4/5, NFR-2356-1/2. GET /v1/directory verifies the device and forwards the upgrade to DIRECTORY.idFromName(userId) with X-Connect-Identity. The DO stores machines(environment_id PK, label, public_key_hex, fingerprint, endpoints_json, server_version, device_id, registered_at, last_seen_at) and meta(key, value) in ctx.storage.sql. hello registers or updates; a new environment id when rows >= maxDevices gets error machine_limit with FREE_MACHINE_LIMIT_MESSAGE and close 4009; a second socket for the same id closes the first with 4011; forget deletes a row and closes that socket with 4012; any change broadcasts directory; hello answers welcome. Fingerprint = first 10 bytes of SHA-256 of the key as five groups of four hex, via WebCrypto. Pure reducer in directory-state.ts (share room-state pattern), decoder in protocol.ts (known keys only, 64 KiB, label <= 64 chars, <= 16 endpoints), and log.ts is the only logging function and writes only frame type, environment id and outcome. ping/pong via setWebSocketAutoResponse.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-6, D-2356-6, D-2356-9 limits. signal frames are forwarded to the target socket with from stamped from the sender socket attachment (never from the frame); an offline target answers error peer_offline with the session. Frame caps: 64 KiB frame, 32 KiB SDP, 2 KiB candidate. purpose approval signals pass only between the requester of a live approval and its target (or any other account machine when to is null), else error approval_unknown. ice-servers relay false answers STUN_URLS split on commas. approval-request stores approvals(request_id PK, from_env, to_env, created_at, expires_at) and forwards to the target or every other online machine; limits 1 pending per requester, 5 per account (error approval_limit), 10-minute expiry checked on read; welcome also delivers live approvals targeting that socket; approval-cancel deletes and forwards.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7, D-2356-12. turn.ts copies services/share/src/turn.ts with TURN_TTL_SECONDS = 600. relay_usage(month PK, bytes) keyed by UTC YYYY-MM. ice-servers relay true refuses in order: relay_not_allowed (plan free), relay_cap_reached (month total >= cap), turn_unavailable (secrets unset); otherwise returns TURN iceServers. relay-usage adds bytes (integer 0..1e9, else bad_frame); when the total first reaches the cap, broadcast relay-status stopped true. A new month starts a fresh row. welcome includes the current RelayStatus. Optional Worker var RELAY_CAP_BYTES (positive integer) overrides RELAY_MONTHLY_CAP_BYTES; unset or invalid uses the constant.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-8, D-2356-13/14/15/18, D-20. Tables inboxes(inbox_id PK, secret_hash UNIQUE, environment_id, created_at) and inbox_events(event_id PK, inbox_id, environment_id, received_at, size, next_attempt_at, sealed BLOB). inbox-create (refused plan_required on free) returns inbox-created with url PUBLIC_BASE_URL/h/<doId>.<secret> (doId = 64-hex DO id, secret 32 hex) and stores only SHA-256(secret). POST /h/:id: split on the dot, idFromString(doId) (invalid -> 404 not found), constant-time hash compare (wrong -> identical 404), read at most 262_144 bytes while streaming (413), per-inbox 200 pending and per-account 64 MiB caps (429 Retry-After 3600), INBOX_LIMIT 120/min, plan free -> 403; seal the D-2356-15 JSON with sealTo to the owner machine key, insert, answer 202 { queued: true }, push inbox-event if the machine is online. inbox-ack deletes; inbox-nack sets next_attempt_at = now + max(retryAfter, 60 s) and arms the alarm; welcome sends all pending in received_at order; alarm deletes rows older than 24 h and re-sends due rows. inbox-delete only by the owning machine. forget of a machine (WI-5) also deletes that machine's inboxes and their pending events.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-10, D-2356-11, NFR-2356-5. Add "werift": "0.25.1" exactly. RtcTransport(port: RtcSignalingPort, onIncoming) with dial(peerEnvironmentId, { relay, purpose, signal }) -> Promise<Duplex> and close(peer?). One RTCPeerConnection per (peer, relay) reused; each dial opens a new ordered reliable data channel labelled ovdl; offer/answer/ICE through port.send/onSignal; iceServers from port.iceServers(relay); relay uses iceTransportPolicy relay on the initiator only; abort rejects. rtc-duplex.ts wraps a data channel as a Duplex: writes split into <= 16 KiB chunks, pause while bufferedAmount > 1 MiB and resume on bufferedamountlow (threshold 256 KiB), destroy closes the channel, close/end emitted on channel close, remoteAddress rtc:<first 16 hex>. Implementation checkpoint: after npm run build confirm dist/dashboard/server.js loads werift; fallback is neverBundle werift in both tsdown configs plus the desktop server-resources lists (PRD WI-10).

narrative.Action: PRD WI-13, D-2356-9/10, D-18. wire.ts: ChannelMode gains approval, MODE_BYTES.approval = 0x03, the preamble appends the 16-byte request id for approval mode as for pairing. noise.ts: pattern union gains XX; xxInitiator/xxResponder; prologueFor("approval", requestId); approvalSas(handshakeHash) = (uint32BE(SHA-256("overdeck-approve-sas/1" || 0x00 || hash)[0..4]) mod 1_000_000) zero-padded to 6 digits and formatted "123 456". open.ts: OpenChannelOptions gains { mode: "approval", localKey, requestId }. accept.ts: AcceptChannelOptions.takeApproval?(requestId) -> boolean, refusal 03 when false, single use. channel-socket.ts: marker carries approvalSas. remote-request-gate.ts: APPROVAL_CHANNEL_ALLOWLIST = GET /api/environment and POST /api/machines/approval-exchange; an approval channel reaches only those (401 otherwise); POST /api/machines/approval-exchange from any non-approval socket answers 401 (before/after in the PRD). Implementation checkpoint: noise-handshake@4.2.0 accepts XX; fallback XXpsk0 with psk = SHA-256("overdeck-approve-psk/1" || 0x00 || requestId); record which shipped in docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md.
